A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same Conformal Linguistic Calibration work. Their text, equations, figures, tables, and complete appendices are readable and support reliable comparison despite substantial reformatting.

before.justification: V1 reports original CLC experiments on SimpleQA and Natural Questions, fine-tuned claim-rewriting results on CORE/FActScore, and generated examples.

after.justification: V2 retains these empirical experiments and adds abstention comparisons, informativeness measurements, and manual validation of belief summaries.

M1.justification: The answer-sampling, clustering, multiplicity-based nesting, belief-rewriting, and LTT-calibration pipeline remains unchanged, as do the SFT/DPO/ORPO training approaches. New masking and scoring components serve evaluation rather than modify CLC.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate SimpleQA, short non-yes/no Natural Questions, and CORE/FActScore biography claims. The new informativeness and manual checks analyse retained data without adding a benchmark, domain, or evaluated user population.

E2.justification: V2 adds confidence-threshold abstention to both QA factuality comparisons in Figure 3. V1's naive-rewriting factuality comparison on NQ disappears; naive rewriting instead participates in the new CPMI comparisons. The GPT-4o reference and base/SFT/DPO/ORPO comparisons remain.

E3.justification: V2 adds abstention-versus-CLC percentage matching, CPMI evaluation with personal-entity masking, and manual entailment judging of 55 sampled questions with two exclusions. These substantially expand evaluation design. The abstention paragraph inconsistently describes its percentage as answering versus backing off, limiting precise interpretation.

E4.justification: New Section 4.2 quantitatively tests whether increasing multiplicity reduces informativeness, while Section 3.1 adds manual checking of whether summaries faithfully describe answer sets. V1's two main-text Table 1 examples are removed; the larger appendix example collection is retained.

E5.justification: Figure 4 newly reports 95% confidence-interval shading for CPMI. V1's shaded regions represent conformal guarantees rather than these empirical intervals. V2 does not explain the interval calculation or newly specify repeated-run or seed counts.

E6.justification: V2 adds abstention curves showing a large CLC advantage on SimpleQA but no uniform superiority on NQ, decreasing CLC informativeness curves, and manual precision 0.81 and recall 0.91. V1's naive NQ factuality points and two illustrative examples are removed. Retained CLC and fine-tuning curves preserve their earlier trends.

T1.justification: The possible-world definitions, LTT formulation, Theorem 3.2, and its proof remain substantively unchanged. Agent-indexed notation and renamed cluster/theorem variables clarify the existing mathematics; the proof moves from Appendix B to C.

C1.justification: The central calibration and adaptive-rewriting contributions remain. V2 explicitly qualifies the GPT-4o comparison as higher factuality through less specific answers and strengthens the conclusion's contrast with prior risk-control approaches by emphasizing answering every question with steady factuality improvement.

C2.justification: V2 interprets tight calibration as avoiding trivially true answers and explicitly motivates fine-tuning as amortizing the costly sampling pipeline. It interprets the manual check as supporting summary validity while identifying subjective cases. The existing limitation concerning unguaranteed nesting remains.

D1.justification: V2 adds two-A100-80GB hardware information, estimator and masking-model details, dataset sources/licenses, and a planned Hugging Face release statement. Conversely, it omits v1's explicit 4,289-question NQ count, equal random NQ split, and calibration risk grid. These are documentation changes, not established experimental reruns.

R1.justification: V2 adds prediction-set references such as Cresswell et al. and Kumar et al., plus informativeness-related references including Sap et al. and Wang et al. Several factuality-enhancement citations, including RARR and DoLa, disappear. The substantive related-work review is largely retained in Appendix A.

P1.justification: The introduction is substantially rewritten around two approaches to uncertainty communication. Separate SimpleQA and NQ sections are merged, related work moves into the appendix, and the experimental narrative is reorganized. A submission checklist and impact/license appendices are added.

P2.justification: The main text changes from two columns to one, with widespread resizing and reflow of displays. Figure 3 receives revised axes, legends, and captions; Figure 4 is added; v1 Table 1 is removed; and appendix tables are resized with relocated captions.

improvement.justification: V2 substantially strengthens evidence for the central factuality-specificity trade-off. V1 lacked a quantitative informativeness assessment and direct abstention comparison; v2 adds both, plus manual checking of belief-summary fidelity. These address important validation gaps. Ambiguous comparison percentages, unexplained confidence intervals, and omitted calibration details limit reproducibility, but the added evidence provides a substantial net improvement.
